descriptions.title: Why a proxy exists at all
descriptions.body: The whole app is one HTML file that can run straight off disk (file://). But a file:// page is CORS-blocked from calling ESPN, Kalshi, OpenRouter, or Ollama directly. The FastAPI proxy solves this by fetching every external source SERVER-SIDE and serving the HTML itself at GET / — so when you use the app at http://localhost:8710/ everything is same-origin and 'just works'. This is also what makes the portable .exe self-contained: the proxy is bundled inside it and the app loads from the proxy, not from disk. Open the HTML alone and you get a degraded, no-live-data fallback; open it through the proxy and you get the full tool.

descriptions.title: No database — a cache, not a store
descriptions.body: Gamez deliberately has no SQL database. State that must persist on the server is just the latest fetched-and-scored snapshot, held in an in-memory dict (CACHE) under a threading.Lock and mirrored to data/cache.json so a restart warm-starts with last-good data. The EA FC 26 ratings CSV is cached weekly on disk. Everything user-specific — manual scores, the chosen bet, AI provider + keys, Kalshi paste, workspace layout — lives in the browser's localStorage, never on the server. The one external DB it touches is read-only: it reads the shared OpenRouter key out of Maia's maia.db.

descriptions.title: EA FC 26 as the squad-strength stand-in
descriptions.body: The realistic problem in mid-2026 is that the actual World Cup squads aren't published until just before the tournament, so API-Football returns 0 players for the 2026 season. Rather than show nothing, the default player_source is 'fifa': it downloads EA FC 26's player ratings (free, no key, no quota), maps each player's club-derived 'overall' to their NATIONAL team, prefers genuine national-team members, and feeds those 0-100 ratings straight into the squad-strength aggregation via score_all_rated(). When the real 2026 squads appear, flipping player_source to 'apifootball' swaps in real match-stat-derived scores through the percentile engine — no other change.

descriptions.title: The locked betting-window math
descriptions.body: The model has a fixed, documented shape that is intentionally not changed casually. A single per-match win probability p (from squad strength married with form) is raised to the number of rounds a team must survive to win a bet placed at a given phase: winProb = p^rounds (ROUNDS = Group 6 … Final 1). payout = 1/(winProb + fee). An information-quality weight INFO (0.15 at Group rising to 1.0 at the Final) reflects how much is actually known by each phase, and value = info × min(1, (1/winProb − 1)/5) combines payout potential with information. The result is a structural lens — R16/QF is the sweet spot — not a prediction, and a disclaimer to that effect is surfaced in every payload.

descriptions.title: Server-side keys and the tunnel gate
descriptions.body: No secret is ever hardcoded in the HTML. Cloud-provider keys a user pastes live only in their browser's localStorage and go only to the provider they picked. The shared OpenRouter key lives server-side (config.json or maia.db) and the browser calls /ai/openrouter without ever seeing it. Because the same proxy is exposed publicly via the Cloudflare tunnel, the shared AI can be gated: _via_tunnel() detects Cloudflare request headers, and when ai_access_password is set, only tunnel traffic carrying a matching X-AI-Access header is served — the owner's own local/exe use is never gated. The password is re-read per request, so changing it locks out stale users instantly. The local-only config endpoints refuse to serve config.json over the tunnel at all.

descriptions.title: One codebase, three ways to run, packaged to share
descriptions.body: The same files run as (1) the raw HTML from disk, (2) the proxy serving the app at localhost for full functionality, or (3) a portable PyInstaller app that bundles the proxy and opens in its own native window via pywebview. The build is OS-aware (WC2026-{win,mac,linux}) because a Windows .exe can't run on mac/linux, and GitHub Actions builds all three. The bundled config is key-sanitized so a shared binary never leaks the owner's keys; a friend either pastes their own key, uses the shared tunnel AI behind an access code, or installs a free local Ollama (guided by the /setup page).
